You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).

- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: F has only one route around the wall. Handle it last so it doesn't block A's path.
move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).

Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a grid rearrangement puzzle.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where each object must end up.
You control ALL objects on the board: A, B, C, D, E, F. You may move any of them on any turn.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.

SCRATCHPAD:
Each turn, the `message:` line is a scratchpad for your own thinking. Use it to reason before you commit to a move. 
Sketch a plan, note which object to handle next, flag walls or other objects in the way, or leave yourself a reminder. 
Your previous turns (both your messages and your moves) stay in the conversation, so anything you write here is visible to you on later turns: treat it as a running memory to carry plans forward across the game.
Keep it to a single line, immediately followed by your `move:` line.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble or thinking text before it.
message: <a brief note to yourself, a scratchpad for plans, observations, or reminders. Visible to you on later turns. It does not affect the game mechanics.>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A right

The game ends automatically as soon as every object is on its target cell.

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
